reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program
    Jurisdiction: Massachusetts
    Focus year: 2021

    Question: In an eviction action, can a tenant rebut/raise the defense that eviction is unlawful
    because it was motivated by a legally recognized form of discrimination?
*/

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Scenario facts (translate the question's factual statement)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

state(massachusetts).
focus_year(2021).

eviction_action(case1).
tenant(tenant1).
landlord(landlord1).
party_in_case(tenant1, case1).
party_in_case(landlord1, case1).

% The tenant seeks to raise a defense: eviction is unlawful due to discriminatory motivation.
defense_claimed(tenant1, case1, discriminatory_motivation).

/* scenario_statement/0 succeeds when the encoded scenario is satisfied. */
scenario_statement :-
    state(massachusetts),
    focus_year(2021),
    eviction_action(case1),
    tenant(tenant1),
    party_in_case(tenant1, case1),
    defense_claimed(tenant1, case1, discriminatory_motivation).

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Statute translations (as deterministic predicates), per provided statutes
----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

% [1] MA Gen L ch 281  2 (2021)
% Effect: general laws provisions that are the same as existing statutes are construed as a continuation,
% not as new enactments; references to revised/re-enacted provisions construed to apply to incorporated provisions.
statute_ma_gl_ch281_s2_continuation_of_existing_statutes(massachusetts, 2021).

/* Deterministic helper capturing the core construction rule. */
legal_construe_general_laws_as_continuation(State, Year, yes) :-
    statute_ma_gl_ch281_s2_continuation_of_existing_statutes(State, Year),
    !.
legal_construe_general_laws_as_continuation(_State, _Year, no) :-
    !.

% [2] MA Gen L ch 279  8a (2021)
% Effect: for determining effective time of a consecutive sentence, prior sentence deemed expired upon parole/release;
% nothing alters/controls Ch 127  131 or 149.
statute_ma_gl_ch279_s8a_prior_sentence_deemed_expired_on_release(massachusetts, 2021).
statute_ma_gl_ch279_s8a_does_not_alter_ch127_131_or_149(massachusetts, 2021).

/* Deterministic predicate: prior sentence deemed expired when prisoner is released (parole or otherwise),
   but only for the purpose of determining the taking effect time of a consecutive sentence. */
legal_prior_sentence_deemed_expired_for_consecutive_timing(State, Year, ReleaseType, yes) :-
    statute_ma_gl_ch279_s8a_prior_sentence_deemed_expired_on_release(State, Year),
    ( ReleaseType = parole
    ; ReleaseType = otherwise
    ),
    !.
legal_prior_sentence_deemed_expired_for_consecutive_timing(_State, _Year, _ReleaseType, no) :-
    !.

% [3] MA Gen L ch 278a  18 (2021)
% Effect: order allowing/denying motion for forensic/scientific analysis under that chapter is final and appealable;
% if moving party appeals a denial, notice of appeal within 30 days after entry of judgment.
statute_ma_gl_ch278a_s18_forensic_order_final_and_appealable(massachusetts, 2021).
statute_ma_gl_ch278a_s18_notice_of_appeal_within_days(massachusetts, 2021, 30).

/* Deterministic predicate: appeal deadline in days for denial of motion under Ch 278A. */
legal_ch278a_appeal_deadline_days(State, Year, Days) :-
    statute_ma_gl_ch278a_s18_notice_of_appeal_within_days(State, Year, Days),
    !.

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Apply reasoning to the scenario
----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

% The provided statutes are not eviction/housing anti-discrimination statutes and do not create
% a tenant defense in an eviction action based on discriminatory motivation.
%
% We encode the mapping explicitly: these statutes create no such eviction defense.
statute_creates_eviction_defense(State, Year, _Defense) :-
    % If any provided statute created an eviction defense, we would capture it here.
    % None of the provided statutes do so.
    legal_construe_general_laws_as_continuation(State, Year, yes),
    fail.
statute_creates_eviction_defense(State, Year, _Defense) :-
    legal_prior_sentence_deemed_expired_for_consecutive_timing(State, Year, parole, yes),
    fail.
statute_creates_eviction_defense(State, Year, _Defense) :-
    legal_ch278a_appeal_deadline_days(State, Year, 30),
    fail.

% A defense is "legally recognized" for this QA only if some encoded statute provides it.
legally_recognized_defense(State, Year, Defense) :-
    statute_creates_eviction_defense(State, Year, Defense).

% Tenant may raise the defense in the eviction action only if the defense is legally recognized in the encoded law.
tenant_may_raise_defense_in_eviction(Case, Tenant, Defense) :-
    eviction_action(Case),
    tenant(Tenant),
    party_in_case(Tenant, Case),
    defense_claimed(Tenant, Case, Defense),
    state(State),
    focus_year(Year),
    legally_recognized_defense(State, Year, Defense).

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   housing_answer/1 (must be deterministic; Result is yes or no)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

housing_answer(Result) :-
    scenario_statement,
    ( tenant_may_raise_defense_in_eviction(case1, tenant1, discriminatory_motivation) ->
        Result = yes
    ;
        Result = no
    ),
    !.

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Main entrypoint (required)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).
